summary: RAG demos + over-count(8) dedup on adapter v2a_e1
hypothesis: Stacking exp040's corpus-RAG few-shot demos (which targeted coverage/specificity) with exp046's over-count(8)+dedup (which targeted non-redundancy) should be additive and push quality above the 0.430 champion, because the two add-ons were believed to act on independent rubric axes.
technique: A single greedy call on the champion v2a_e1 adapter with both perturbations layered: exp040-style corpus RAG exemplars injected into the system prompt, plus exp046-style over-generation of 8 candidates followed by deterministic Swift dedup down to 7.
result: Scored 0.395 on the full-30 greedy eval (3 wins / 1 tie / 25 losses vs Sonnet, 1 refusal) — a real regression of −0.035 below the champion exp046 (0.430) and also below corpus-RAG-only exp040 (0.405). Rubric: atom 4 / spec 4 / coverage 3 / nonRed 3 (fell from exp046's 4) / nat 4. The hypothesis was falsified: the corpus demo block perturbed the count-8 generation enough that the dedup pass could no longer suppress the single clean redundant pair it reliably fixed in exp046, while simultaneously introducing new redundancies it couldn't reach — the two add-ons compounded and cancelled rather than adding. Discarded; champion remains exp046.
